Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, west Triangle, Quezon City http: //www. dilg_gov.ph DILG OPINION No. 80 s. 2022 AUG 11 2022 Atty. VENUS C. VELASCO Sangguniang Panlungsod Secretary Municipality of Cabuyao Province of Laguna Dear Atty. Velasco: This has reference to your letter dated 07 March 2022 seeking legal opinion from this Department on the following: 1. Whether or not the regular session conducted by members of the Sanggunian Panlungsod is valid even without any notice or invitation indicating the agenda for the said meeting. 2. If so, is the resolution or ordinance approved or passed during such session also valid? Per your representation, on January 24, 2022, eight (8) members of the Sangguniang Panlungsod and the Vice-Mayor, as the presiding officer, conducted the regular session regarding the proposed annual budget without any notice or invitation indicating the agenda for the said session to other sanggunian members. You mentioned that during said regular session, the Sangguniang Panlungsod discussed the proposed annual budget and invited the Local Finance Committee to clarify matters related therein since the proposed annual budget for 2022 of the City of Cabuyao was returned to the Office of the Mayor. You also represented that as a result of the session on January 24, 2022, the Sanggunian has no agenda for the conduct of Regular Sessions from January 31, 2022 as there are no other matters that may be discussed, in reference to the mandate of Section 323 of the Local Government Code providing for 90 days period wherein no other matters shall be taken up during the sessions except for the passing of the Annual Budget ordinance. Further, you alleged that there was no due process to the other members of the sanggunian comprising the minority bloc. Hence, the queries. We will answer the queries in one discussion since they are interrelated. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Relevant to the issues at hand is Section 52 of R.A. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991, thus: "SECTION 52. Sessions. — (a) On the first dav of the session immediately followinq the election of its members. the sanqqunian shall. by resolution. fix the day. time. and place of its regular sessions. The minimum number of regular sessions shall be once a week for the sangguniang panlalawigan, sangguniang panlungsod, and sangguniang bayan, and twice a month for the sangguniang barangay. (b) When public interest so demands, special sessions may be called by the local chief executive or by a majority of the members of the sanggunian. (c) All sanggunian sessions shall be open to the public unless a closed-door session is ordered by an affirmative vote of majority of the members present, there being a quorum, in the public interest or for reasons of security, decency, or morality. No two (2) sessions, regular or special, may be held in a single day. (d) In the case of special sessions of the sanqqunian. a written notice to the members shall be served personally at the member's usual place of residence at least twentv-four (24) hours before the special session is held. Unless otherwise concurred in by two-thirds (2/3) vote of the sanggunian members present, there being a quorum, no other matters may be considered at a special session except those stated in the notice. (e) Each sanggunian shall keep a journal and record of its proceedings which may be published upon resolution of the sanggunian concerned." Based on the aforequoted Section 52 (a), there is no necessity for the issuance of written notice and invitation to the sanggunian members prior to the conduct of every regular session since the day, time, and place thereof have already been fixed in a resolution adopted on the first day of the session immediately following the election of its members. "To notify" means to inform someone and "to invite" means to request someone to do something. Since the sanggunian members themselves adopted the resolution fixing the day, time, and place of their regular sessions, there is nothing to inform them about. As a consequence, the sanggunian members cannot therefore use good faith as a defense for not attending the regular sessionl. It is only in the case of special sessions that written notice to the sanggunian members is necessary. Going now to the issue on the failure of the sanggunian to notify its members about the agenda to be taken in a particular regular session, please be reminded that the submission of matters to be included in the agenda, the manner of distributing thereof, and the period within which to distribute the agenda are all governed by the sanggunian's duly adopted Internal Rules of Procedure (IRP). Section 50 of the LGC provides, viz: 1 DILG Legal Opinion No. 61, series of 2010. page 2 of 4

"SECTION 50. Intemal Rules of Procedure. — (a) On the first regular session following the election of its members and within ninety (90) days thereafter, the sanggunian concerned shall adopt or update its existing rules of procedure. (b) The rules of procedure shall provide for the following: (1) The organization of the sanggunian and the election of its officers as well as the creation of standing committees which shall include, but shall not be limited to, the committees on appropriations, women and family, human rights, youth and sports development, environmental protection, and cooperatives; the general jurisdiction of each committee; and the election of the chairman and members of each committee; (2) The order and calendar of business for each session: (3) The legislative process; (4) The parliamentary procedures which include the conduct of members 2during sessions; (5) The discipline of members for disorderly behavior and absences without justifiable cause for four (4) consecutive sessions, for which they may be censured, reprimanded, or excluded from the session, suspended for not more than sixty (60) days, or expelled: Provided, That the penalty of suspension or expulsion shall require the concurrence of at least two-thirds (2/3) vote of all the sanggunian members: Provided, further, That a member convicted by final judgment to imprisonment of at least one (1) year for any crime involving moral turpitude shall be automatically expelled from the sanggunian; and (6) Such other rules as the sanggunian may adopt." (Emphasis and underlining supplied) Failure to distribute the agenda for that particular regular session is considered a violation or non-compliance of the sanggunian's IRP. For this, the ruling of the Supreme Court in Romulo E. Yfiiquez is instructive, thus: "Rules of parliamentary practice are merely procedure and not substantive. The rules of procedure adopted bv deliberative bodies have not the force of a public taw. but they are merely in the nature of by-laws. prescribed for the orderlv and convenient conduct of their own proceedinqs. The rules adopted by deliberative bodies are subject to revocation, modification, or waiver at the pleasure of the body adopting them. xxx." (underlining ours) Hence, the regular session as well as the resolutions and/or ordinances approved or passed during said session where no agenda were distributed are still valid. However, those who are found to have deliberately violated the period and manner of distributing 2 141 SCRA 263. page 3 Of 4

the agenda may be proceeded against for violation of your sanggunian's IRP. Let it be stressed that sanggunian members are bound to observe and respect their duly adopted IRPs. Be that as it may, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have sufficiently addressed your concerns. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: Un ers GAN ary for Local Government OUSLG/MLl/LLLS-LRALLD/lasm/clp copy furnish: DIR. ARIEL O.
